headline_marked: PM reportedly asks State Minister Ishraque to resign after firearm display
headline: PM reportedly asks State Minister Ishraque to resign after firearm display
summary: Ishraque Hossain's position in the cabinet is uncertain following public outrage over his armed participation in an anti-drug operation. Sources claim the Prime Minister has demanded his resignation.
details: State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain's tenure is in doubt after reports emerged that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman asked him to resign. The demand reportedly followed public outcry over Ishraque's display of a firearm during an "anti-drug operation" in Dhaka's Gendaria on Saturday.

Sources close to the government indicated that Tarique summoned Ishraque after a cabinet meeting and instructed him to step down. While an official statement was pending, state broadcaster BTV initially reported the Prime Minister's order via news ticker, only for Ishraque's office to deny the reports as "rumours" and "baseless".

The controversy has caused embarrassment for the government, raising concerns about ministerial conduct. Tarique also reportedly reprimanded Ishraque for brandishing the firearm and instructed him to apologize publicly. However, Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Ghani declined to comment on the matter when questioned by reporters.

Ishraque himself posted on Facebook that any directive from the Prime Minister is conventionally binding. He stated that if any decision concerning his ministry or himself is made, the nation will be informed officially. His press officer had earlier issued a statement calling the resignation reports "fabricated and motivated".

Government sources revealed that Tarique expressed strong dissatisfaction with Ishraque's actions, questioning his personal involvement in the operation while armed. The incident has led to unease among party members and fears of damaging the government's image, both domestically and internationally.
The controversy began when videos surfaced on Ishraque's verified Facebook page showing him with a pistol during an apprehension near the Dayaganj Ghuntighar railway crossing.

headline_marked: 10 killed as [[unauthorised resort burns down]] in Cox’s Bazar
headline: 10 killed as unauthorised resort burns down in Cox’s Bazar
summary: The TUPTUP Resto & Resort operated without fire licenses or development approval, despite repeated warnings from authorities.
details: A devastating fire at TUPTUP Resto & Resort in Inani, Cox’s Bazar, has killed at least 10 people. Family members are now providing DNA samples to identify the victims, while four members of a family from Jessore remain missing.

The resort was an illegal entity, operating without approval from the deputy commissioner, local union council, or municipal authorities. It was also built in a designated no-development zone where such constructions are prohibited.

The Fire Service and Civil Defence department had served a written notice to the resort in June to apply for a fire license, but the establishment failed to comply. The Cox's Bazar Development Authority had also issued removal directives in 2023 and 2024.
A Fire Service official revealed a critical shortage of staff, stating that only one inspector is assigned to monitor 500 to 600 commercial establishments across the entire Cox's Bazar district.

According to officials, nearly 400 commercial establishments in the district are operating without a valid fire license. This structural constraint makes regular safety verifications nearly impossible.
The manager of the resort has been arrested, and the owners have been accused in a legal case following the blaze.
